high.title: Natura (NATU3) leads Ibovespa gains and RD Saúde (RADL3) is worst performing stock; see week highlights
high.summary: The Ibovespa completed its second consecutive week of gains, rising 3.58% to close at 188,042.02 points amid uncertainties about the Iran conflict duration and Brazil's electoral scenario. The USD/BRL closed at R$ 5.1599, with the dollar weakening 1.56% against the real during the week. Central Bank President Gabriel Galípolo explained the smaller interest rate cut (Selic from 15% to 14.75%) was designed to "gain more time" to assess the scenario. Galípolo stated that "the cushion accumulated with a more conservative position allowed us to gain time to better understand the scenario and continue with the planned trajectory." The market remains focused on Middle East conflict implications for monetary policy and the emerging electoral landscape. This cautious BCB approach suggests potential for more gradual easing ahead, supporting BRL strength and providing clarity on the monetary policy trajectory for bond investors.

high.title: Oil falls after little-changed start as market assesses war-related disruptions
high.summary: Oil prices declined on Monday after a flat opening, with Brent futures falling 1.05% to US$ 107.9/barrel and WTI dropping 1.71% to US$ 109.6/barrel. This follows dramatic gains in the previous session (WTI +11%, Brent +8%), marking the largest absolute price increases since 2020. Investors are awaiting clarity on US-Iran talks while remaining cautious about prolonged supply losses from maritime transport disruptions. Trump escalated pressure on Tehran with social media threats over the Easter weekend. For Brazilian markets, sustained high oil prices are positive for Petrobras revenues and dividend prospects, supporting both PETR4 shares and the real through improved trade balance dynamics.

medium.title: Dividends: Itaú BBA swaps Aura Minerals (AURA33) for Petrobras (PETR4) in April; see stocks
medium.summary: Itaú BBA added Petrobras (PETR4) to its dividend portfolio, expecting the company to benefit from higher oil prices through diesel price adjustments. The bank projects stronger revenues will enable generous dividend distributions in coming quarters. The dividend portfolio fell 6.5% in March, underperforming the Ibovespa by 5.8 percentage points, with Bradesco contributing the largest negative impact with a 9% decline.
